all.description: When true, returns all available sports. When false or omitted, returns only recently updated (in-season) sports.

function.name: v4_sports_sport_odds
function.description: Retrieves live and upcoming games with bookmaker odds for a specified sport or across all sports. Returns game details including bookmaker-specific odds formatted by market type. Use this function to get real-time betting data from supported regions and bookmakers.

sport.description: Sport key identifying the sport to query (e.g., 'basketball_nba'). Use 'upcoming' to retrieve the next 8 upcoming games across all sports. Sport keys must match those returned by the /sports endpoint.

regions.description: Comma-separated list of regions to filter bookmakers (e.g., 'us,uk'). Each region will count as 1 request against your API quota. See documentation for region-bookmaker mappings.

oddsformat.description: Format for returned odds values. Select a standardized odds format.

markets.description: Comma-separated list of odds markets to include (e.g., 'h2h,outrights'). Each market will count as 1 request against your API quota. Common markets include 'h2h' (head-to-head), 'spreads', and 'totals'.

dateformat.description: Format for returned timestamps in game data.

function.name: v4_sports_sport_scores
function.description: Retrieves live, upcoming, and optionally recent completed games with scores for a specified sport. Currently in beta for select sports; refer to the [sports list](https://the-odds-api.com/sports-odds-data/sports-apis.html) for available options.

sport.description: Sport key identifying the specific sport to retrieve game data for. Must match a supported sport key from the API's available sports list.

daysfrom.description: Optional number of days in the past (valid values: 1-3) to include completed games in the response. If omitted, only live and upcoming games are included.

function.name: calculate_etf
function.description: Calculates the theoretical equity asset percentage change for a leveraged ETF based on its leverage factor and the underlying asset's percentage change. This function is useful for financial analysis of leveraged investment products.

leverage.description: The ETF's leverage factor relative to the underlying asset (e.g., 2 for 2x leverage, 3 for 3x leverage). This determines how strongly the ETF responds to the underlying asset's movements.

underlying.description: The percentage change of the underlying asset as a whole number (e.g., 5 for 5%, -2 for -2%). This represents the base asset's performance before applying leverage.

function.name: leveraged_equity_calculator
function.description: Calculates the projected equity value after a price change for a leveraged investment. This function helps analyze leveraged ETF performance by quantifying the impact of leverage on equity growth or decline based on underlying asset price movements.

leverage.description: The leverage multiplier applied to the investment. For example, 2 for 2x leverage. Higher values amplify both gains and losses.

originalshareprice.description: The initial price of the underlying asset before the price change. Must be a positive integer.

originalequity.description: The initial investment amount at the start of the period. Must be a positive integer.

projectedshareprice.description: The expected future price of the underlying asset. Must be a positive integer.

function.name: get_one_grand_prix_race_winner
function.description: Retrieves detailed information about a Grand Prix race winner, including rider name, team, race statistics, and finishing position when available. Useful for motorsport data analysis or historical racing information queries.

accept_encoding.description: Preferred encoding format for the response data. Common values may include 'gzip' for compressed responses or 'json' for standard JSON format.

is_id.description: Unique numerical identifier of the Grand Prix race to retrieve winner information for. Must be a positive integer corresponding to a valid race ID in the database.

function.name: get_one_podium
function.description: Retrieves detailed podium information for a specific MotoGP race entry. Returns data about race results, standings, or achievements associated with the specified podium ID.

accept_encoding.description: HTTP Accept-Encoding header value indicating supported content encodings (e.g., 'gzip, deflate'). Used to negotiate compressed response payloads.

is_id.description: Unique numerical identifier of the podium entry to retrieve. This ID corresponds to a specific race result or achievement in the MotoGP database.

function.name: search_champions
function.description: Searches for motorcycle racing champions based on various criteria including season, rider, country, constructor, and racing class. Returns matching champion records with associated metadata.

accept_encoding.description: HTTP Accept-Encoding header value for response compression. Required for compatibility with server compression settings. Example: 'gzip, deflate'

season.description: Year or season identifier (e.g., '2023', 'MotoGP Season 12'). Leave empty to include results from all seasons.

country.description: Country name or ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (e.g., 'Spain', 'ES'). Leave empty to include all countries.

constructor.description: Name of the vehicle constructor/manufacturer (e.g., 'Honda', 'Yamaha'). Leave empty to include all constructors.

rider.description: Full name of the rider or competitor (e.g., 'Valentino Rossi'). Leave empty to include all riders.

function.name: search_fastest_laps
function.description: Retrieves fastest lap records from MotoGP race data filtered by rider name and/or country of origin. Returns structured data containing rider details, country codes, lap times, and race metadata. Useful for performance analysis and historical comparisons in motorsports.

accept_encoding.description: Compression encoding method for the response (required by API infrastructure). Valid values: 'gzip', 'deflate', 'identity', or empty string for default compression.

rider.description: Rider name filter (case-insensitive partial matches supported). Omit or set to empty string for no rider filter.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code filter (e.g., 'ES' for Spain, 'AU' for Australia). Set to empty string for no country filter.

function.name: search_grand_prix_race_winners
function.description: Retrieves Grand Prix race winner data filtered by rider, circuit, class, constructor, country, or season. Returns historical race results including winners, teams, and race details.

accept_encoding.description: The encoding type for the response. Example values include 'gzip', 'deflate', or 'identity'.

constructor.description: Name of the motorcycle constructor/manufacturer (e.g., 'Honda', 'Yamaha', 'Ducati'). Case-sensitive. If omitted, returns results across all constructors.

season.description: Year representing the racing season (e.g., '2023', '2022'). If omitted, returns results from all seasons.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code (e.g., 'IT' for Italy, 'FR' for France) or full country name matching the race location. Case-insensitive. If omitted, returns results from all countries.

is_class.description: Race class category. Case-sensitive. If omitted, defaults to MotoGP class.

rider.description: Full name of the rider (e.g., 'Valentino Rossi', 'Marc Márquez'). Case-sensitive. If omitted, returns results for all riders.

function.name: search_podiums
function.description: Retrieve MotoGP podium results filtered by rider name or country code. Returns historical podium achievements, race details, and rider statistics. Use this function to find podium finishes by specific riders or nationalities.

accept_encoding.description: Encoding type for the response data. Specify the desired compression format for efficient data transfer.

rider.description: Name of the rider to filter podium results. Partial matches may be supported for flexible searching. Leave empty to return results for all riders.

country.description: ISO country code (e.g., 'US' for United States) to filter podiums by rider nationality. Leave empty to return results for all countries.

function.name: search_poles
function.description: Retrieves motorcycle racing pole position statistics from the MotoGP database. Returns data about race poles earned by specific riders or within specified countries of origin.

accept_encoding.description: Compression encoding for the response to optimize bandwidth usage. Valid values include 'gzip', 'deflate', and 'identity'.

rider.description: Name of the rider to filter results by. If not provided or empty, returns pole statistics for all riders.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code (e.g., 'ITA' for Italy) to filter results by country of origin. If not provided or empty, returns pole statistics for all countries.

language.description: Language code for filtering reviews (e.g., 'en' for English, 'zh' for Chinese). Returns reviews in the specified language if available.

frameposition.description: Page number of reviews to fetch. Used in conjunction with framesize for paginating through multiple sets of reviews.

language.description: Language code for search results (ISO 639-1 format). Determines language of product descriptions and metadata.

framesize.description: Number of items to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100.

imageurl.description: URL of reference image for visual similarity search. Leave empty for text-based search only.

minprice.description: Minimum product price filter (inclusive). Set to 0 to remove lower price limit.

itemtitle.description: Search query term for product title matching. Supports partial matches and fuzzy search.

minvolume.description: Minimum order volume filter (inclusive). Set to 0 to ignore order volume.

maxprice.description: Maximum product price filter (inclusive). Set to -1 to remove upper price limit.

categoryid.description: Restrict results to specific category ID. Leave empty for cross-category search.

orderby.description: Sort criteria for results. Available options: 'price_asc', 'price_desc', 'volume_desc', 'relevance'

function.name: get_race
function.description: Retrieves detailed race results and classification data for cycling competitions. Returns information about race winners, standings, and category-specific classifications. Use this function to analyze race outcomes or obtain historical performance data.

racecategory.description: Race category (e.g., Grand Tour, Classic, Stage Race) - valid values can be obtained from the GET Races endpoint. This defines the classification structure and race type.

race.description: Identifier for the specific race within the category (e.g., 'Tour de France', 'Giro d'Italia'). Must be a valid race name for the specified category.

afterstage.description: Stage number after which to retrieve classification data. Valid values are positive integers up to the total number of stages in the race. Omitting returns overall classification.

year.description: Year of the race (e.g., '2023'). If not specified, defaults to the current year.

classification.description: Type of classification data to retrieve. Valid options include GC (General Classification), Points, KOM (King of Mountains), Youth, Teams, and Stage.

function.name: get_races
function.description: Retrieves UCI cycling races based on category and year. Returns comprehensive race data including dates, locations, classifications, and event details.

category.description: Race category filter to specify type of events (e.g., professional tours, championships, regional circuits)

year.description: Filter races by calendar year (4-digit format, e.g., '2023'). When omitted, defaults to current year data.

function.name: get_riders
function.description: Retrieves comprehensive cyclist data from the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) database, including professional riders, their career statistics, and team affiliations. Useful for sports analytics, historical research, and cycling enthusiast applications.

year.description: Optional four-digit year (e.g., '2023') to filter cyclists active during a specific season. When omitted, returns cyclists across all available historical records.

function.name: get_teams
function.description: Retrieves comprehensive data about all UCI-registered professional cycling teams for a specified season. Returns team details including names, riders, performance statistics, and classification information. Useful for sports analytics, team comparisons, and historical cycling data research.

year.description: Season year to retrieve data for, formatted as 'YYYY'. If not specified, defaults to current season data.

function.name: artist_info
function.description: Retrieves detailed information about a music artist from Shazam.com, including name, genres, biographical details, associated images, and active status. This function provides structured artist data for music discovery, content creation, or artist research purposes.

artist_id.description: The unique numeric identifier for the artist on Shazam's platform. This ID can typically be found in Shazam artist URLs or obtained through related API endpoints.

function.name: artist_search
function.description: Searches for artists by name and returns a list of matching artist records. Use this function when you need to find artist information based on a name query with control over result count.

limit.description: Maximum number of artist results to return. Must be a positive integer specifying the desired result count.

artist.description: Name of the artist to search for. This should be a string representing the artist's name or partial name for matching.

function.name: artist_top_tracks
function.description: Retrieves a specified number of top tracks for a given artist from the Shazam database. Returns tracks ordered by popularity, including metadata like title, duration, and chart position.

limit.description: The number of top tracks to return. Typically between 1 and 20. Must be a positive integer.

artist_id.description: The unique numeric identifier of the artist in the Shazam database.

function.name: search_track
function.description: Searches for a specified track and returns a list of similar tracks. This function is useful for discovering music recommendations based on a given song name.

limit.description: Maximum number of similar tracks to return in the response

track.description: Name of the track to search for and find similar songs

function.name: top_track_by_city
function.description: Retrieves the currently most popular track in a specified city using the Shazam API. Returns chart-topping music data based on local popularity metrics. Useful for understanding regional music trends and cultural preferences.

city_name.description: Name of the city for which to retrieve the top track (e.g., 'Los Angeles', 'Tokyo')

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the country containing the city (e.g., 'US' for United States, 'GB' for United Kingdom)

limit.description: Maximum number of top tracks to return (default: 1, maximum: 10)

function.name: track_info
function.description: Retrieves detailed metadata for a specific music track from Shazam's database. Returns information such as title, artist, album, release date, genre, and other available track details. Useful for music identification, metadata lookup, and integration with music recommendation systems.

track_id.description: Unique identifier for the music track in Shazam's database. This ID can be obtained through Shazam's API or mobile application when identifying a song.

function.name: track_recommendations
function.description: Generates recommendations for musically similar tracks based on a specified track. Returns a curated list of related tracks with metadata including title, artist, and match confidence scores.

track_id.description: Unique identifier of the track for which to find similar recommendations. Must be a positive integer representing a valid track in the catalog.

limit.description: Maximum number of similar tracks to return in the response. Valid range: 1-100. Higher values may result in increased latency.

country.description: Two-letter country code (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2) to filter cities by country. If not provided, cities from all countries are considered.

function.name: historical_weather_record

location.description: The address or latitude, longitude of the location. Addresses can be full or partial (city, state, zip code). If using coordinates, the format should be latitude,longitude (decimal degrees).

enddatetime.description: The end date and time for the data request in ISO format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss) using the location's time zone.

startdatetime.description: The start date and time for the data request in ISO format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss) using the location's time zone.

aggregatehours.description: The interval between weather history data points in the output. Supported values are 1 (hourly) or 24 (daily).

unitgroup.description: The unit system for the output data. Supported values are 'us', 'uk', or 'metric'.

contenttype.description: The format of the output data. Supported values are 'json' or 'csv'. Default is 'csv'.

dayendtime.description: Filters the output to records within the specified end time of the day (format: HH:mm:ss). Default is '17:00:00'.

daystarttime.description: Filters the output to records within the specified start time of the day (format: HH:mm:ss). Default is '08:00:00'.

shortcolumnnames.description: If True, returns shorter, abbreviated column names. If False, returns descriptive column names. Useful for programmatic use.

dataset.description: The variable set to use in the response. Defaults to 'full'.

tempunit.description: The temperature unit in the response (e.g., 'C' for Celsius). Defaults to 'C'.

alt.description: The altitude in meters. Defaults to 0.

periods.description: The number of time steps in the response, with a default of 8 and a maximum of 12. Defaults to 8.

windunit.description: The wind speed unit in the response (e.g., 'MS' for meters per second). Defaults to 'MS'.
